name: KlarSchiff - e-mail inbox (Gmail Trigger -> save attachment + info -> Telegram)

nodes.name: Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)
nodes.notes: Choose your Gmail credential. Create a Gmail filter that puts supplier e-mails with documents under the label 'klarschiff-documents'. Test with fictional documents only.

nodes.name: Save attachment to the KlarSchiff inbox
nodes.notes: The path must be the KlarSchiff inbox folder (KLARSCHIFF_INBOX_DIR, default data/inbox/ in the project). With n8n in Docker, mount that folder as /data/klarschiff/inbox. Only the first attachment is saved; duplicate this node for attachment_1, attachment_2.

parameters.jsonOutput: ={{ JSON.stringify({ from: $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.json.from.text, subject: $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.json.subject, received: $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.json.date, origin: '', destination: 'DE' }) }}

nodes.name: Set (e-mail info for the agent)
nodes.notes: Sender, subject and date go next to the file as <file>.meta.json. Origin can be filled by hand later in the app.

options.fileName: =/data/klarschiff/inbox/{{ $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.json.id }}_{{ $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.binary.attachment_0.fileName }}.meta.json

parameters.fileName: =/data/klarschiff/inbox/{{ $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.json.id }}_{{ $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.binary.attachment_0.fileName }}.meta.json

parameters.text: =New supplier documents for KlarSchiff: "{{ $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.json.subject }}" from {{ $('Gmail Trigger (supplier e-mail with documents)').item.json.from.text }}. Open the app -> Inbox -> Check all.

nodes.name: Telegram (tell the team)
nodes.notes: Choose your Telegram credential (bot token from @BotFather) and the team group chat id.

main.node: Save attachment to the KlarSchiff inbox
